app.name: Hexara
app.description: A 3D online strategy board game — claim land, gather resources and be the first to reach the victory target.

nav.themeDark: Dark theme — night on the board

home.heroSubtitle: A fully 3D board, complete rules, 2 to 6 players, and everything configurable.

board.title: Fully custom board
board.text: Board size, terrain distribution, hex numbers and port placement — lay it out by hand or roll it randomly, then share it with a seed code.

threeD.title: Smooth and three-dimensional
threeD.text: The board renders in WebGL with a free camera, soft shadows and animated dice and construction. Quality scales itself down on mobile.

rules.title: The complete rules
rules.text: Development cards, longest road, largest army, 2:1 and 3:1 ports, the robber, discarding — plus optional variants like the friendly robber.

realtime.title: Realtime and durable
realtime.text: Every move is validated on the server. Disconnected? Come back and the game resumes exactly where it was, with a bot covering your seat.

teams.title: Teams or free-for-all
teams.text: Create a room, invite friends with a code, split into teams and play for a shared score.

pwa.title: Install it on your phone
pwa.text: Hexara is a PWA — add it to your home screen and it behaves like a native app.

rules.title: How to play
rules.intro: Every number on this page is read from the game engine itself, so it can never drift from what happens at the table.
rules.goalBody: First to {0} victory points wins. A settlement is 1 point, a city is 2, and the awards and victory-point cards make up the rest. In a team game the score is shared.
rules.setupBody: Each player places a settlement and a road in turn, then another in reverse order. The second settlement pays out its neighbouring tiles immediately. Two settlements can never be adjacent — there must be at least one corner between them.
rules.turnRoll: Roll the dice. Every tile with that number pays its neighbouring settlements and cities — one for a settlement, two for a city. The tile under the robber pays nothing.
rules.turnRobber: A 7 pays nobody: anyone holding more than {0} cards discards half, then you move the robber and steal one card from someone who has a building on that tile.
rules.turnBuild: Build, buy a development card, or trade. Development cards can be played before rolling too.
rules.turnEnd: End your turn; cards you bought this turn become playable from the next one.
rules.pieces: Each player has {0} roads, {1} settlements and {2} cities, and cannot build past that.
rules.tradeBank: The bank takes {0} of one resource for any one you want.
rules.tradePorts: Ports improve that rate: a generic port is 3:1 and a dedicated port is 2:1 — as long as you have a settlement on that corner.
rules.tradePlayers: You can also offer a swap to the other players. Each offer lasts {0} seconds and the first to accept closes it.
rules.cardsIntro: Only one card per turn, and a card bought this turn stays locked until the next one.

card.Knight: Moves the robber and steals a card. It also joins your army.
card.RoadBuilding: Up to two free roads. The second one may extend the first.
card.YearOfPlenty: Any two resources from the bank; they may be the same.
card.Monopoly: Name a resource and everyone hands you every card of it.
card.VictoryPoint: A victory point that stays hidden until the game ends. It is never played, only counted.

rules.longestRoad: Longest road is worth 2 points and needs {0} pieces or more. An opponent's settlement can cut your road in half.
rules.largestArmy: Largest army is worth 2 points and needs {0} knights or more. Both awards move when someone overtakes the holder.
rules.fairTitle: Things that should put you at ease
rules.fairServer: Dice, trades, resource counts and every rule run and are checked on the server. The browser is never the authority.
rules.fairSecrets: Each player's hand is sent only to them; other people's cards never reach your browser at all, so there is nothing to peek at.
rules.fairBot: If someone disconnects or stalls, a bot makes a simple move after the deadline so the game doesn't hang.
